questions.text: Solve √(2kx + 1) = kx – 5 for x in terms of k, where k > 0.
questions.expectedAnswer: x = (6 + 2√3)/k (rejecting (6 – 2√3)/k as it makes kx – 5 negative)
questions.markingGuide: Square both sides: 2kx + 1 = k²x² – 10kx + 25. Rearrange: k²x² – 12kx + 24 = 0. Quadratic formula: x = (12k ± √(144k² – 96k²))/(2k²) = (12k ± 4k√3)/(2k²) = (6 ± 2√3)/k. Check each root against the original equation (RHS must be ≥ 0). For x = (6 + 2√3)/k ≈ 9.46/k, kx – 5 ≈ 4.46 > 0 ✓. For x = (6 – 2√3)/k ≈ 2.54/k, kx – 5 ≈ –2.46 < 0 (extraneous). So x = (6 + 2√3)/k.

questions.text:
The locus described by |z – 3i| = |z + 4| is a straight line.

Find the gradient of that line. Justify your answer.
questions.markingGuide: Let z = x + yi. Then |z – 3i|² = |z + 4|². So x² + (y – 3)² = (x + 4)² + y². Expand: x² + y² – 6y + 9 = x² + 8x + 16 + y². Simplify: –6y + 9 = 8x + 16, so –6y = 8x + 7, i.e. y = –4x/3 – 7/6. Gradient = –4/3.

questions.text:
Consider u = 5 + 3ki and v = 2 + 7ki, where k is a real constant.

Show that w = u/v will not lie on the real axis (y = 0) for any non-zero value of k.
questions.markingGuide: w = (5+3ki)/(2+7ki). Multiply by conjugate: w = (5+3ki)(2–7ki)/((2+7ki)(2–7ki)) = (10+21k²+(6k–35k)i)/(4+49k²) = (10+21k²–29ki)/(4+49k²). Im(w) = –29k/(4+49k²). For w on real axis: Im(w) = 0 → –29k = 0 → k = 0. Since k ≠ 0, w cannot lie on the real axis.

questions.text: Write 1/(4k + 3i) in the form a + bi, in terms of k.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply by conjugate: (4k–3i)/(16k²+9). Real part = 4k/(16k²+9), Imaginary part = –3/(16k²+9).

questions.text: Find the value(s) of r so that x² + 2rx + (r + 2) = 0 has equal roots.

One solution of 2z³ + dz² + 56z – 60 = 0 is z = 3 – i.

If d is real, find d and the other two solutions.
questions.expectedAnswer: d = –18, other solutions z = 3+i and z = 3
questions.markingGuide: z = 3+i also a root. Factor: z²–6z+10. f(z) = 2(z²–6z+10)(z–a). Constant: 2(10)(–a) = –60. a = 3. Expand: 2(z³–3z²–6z²+18z+10z–30) = 2(z³–9z²+28z–30) = 2z³–18z²+56z–60. d = –18. Third root z = 3.

questions.text: Find the value(s) of the real constant d, given that z = 2 + di and z̄ = 5d·z⁻¹.
questions.markingGuide: z̄ = 2 – di. z⁻¹ = (2 – di)/|z|² = (2 – di)/(4 + d²). So 5d·z⁻¹ = 5d(2 – di)/(4 + d²). Setting z̄ = 5d·z⁻¹: 2 – di = 5d(2 – di)/(4 + d²). Provided 2 – di ≠ 0, divide both sides by (2 – di): 1 = 5d/(4 + d²). Therefore 4 + d² = 5d, giving d² – 5d + 4 = 0, i.e. (d – 1)(d – 4) = 0. So d = 1 or d = 4.

questions.text: Solve z⁴ + 81k⁴ = 0, where k is a real constant. Give solutions in polar form in terms of k.
Given that x + 1/x = m, where m is a real constant, find x³ + 1/x³ in terms of m.
questions.markingGuide: (x+1/x)³ = m³. x³+3x+3/x+1/x³ = m³. x³+1/x³+3(x+1/x) = m³. x³+1/x³ = m³–3m.
